request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Tree search is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests on the first run (the tree search test plus the three scenario tests).

**Server**
- **`PersonService.search(sheetId, text)`** goes over the sheet's tree. It reuses the existing `SheetService.tree`, the same "tree" that name clashes already use: the sheet itself, its parent chain and its descendants. Sibling sheets are not included.
- **Matching:** a person matches if their name or one of their aliases contains the text, ignoring case. Leading and trailing spaces in the text are dropped, so a blank search lists everyone.
- **Order:** this sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets sorted by sheet id, each in its own list order.
- **Due-total** comes from `Rollup.figures`, so it matches the figures the sheet shows and audits. A person with no due-total shows `n/a`, and a retired person shows `0.00`.
- **Endpoint:** `PersonController` has a new `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/search?text=…` that returns the sheet id, name and due-total for each match.
- Searching only reads data: it writes nothing to the store or the audit file.

**Front end**
- The new component is in `features/search/search.ts` and sits on the main screen just above the audit viewer. It has the `search-name` input, the `search` button, a `search-count` and one `search-line` per person, in the form `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`.
- Each press clears the old count and lines before asking the server again, so two presses with the same result can still be told apart. Loading a sheet also clears the results.
- A failed request shows a `search-error` alert.

probe.probe_text:
I read the code without changing anything. Paths below are relative to `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/` unless they start with `frontend:` (meaning `src/main/frontend/src/app/`). ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them ### Per claim (`PersonController.ClaimView`, each field labelled with the `data-testid` it is shown in) | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | **amount** (`claim-amount`) | Typed in. With lines it is the sum of qty × unit, rounded half up (`Claim.addLine`). A negative amount is a **correction**: it must name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person (`ClaimService.requireCorrects`). | | **due** (`claim-due`) | `Dues.figure`, in this order:
1. `settledDue` if the claim is settled (frozen).
2. Otherwise the **base** (`Dues.base`). If `bound` (stated and not PENDING), that is `statedDue`; if not, `rateFigure` = amount × the rate's percent ÷ 100, to 2 decimals.
3. A correction stops at the base: no floor, no late charge.
4. Otherwise add the `lateCharge` while `overdue`, then raise it to the **floor** in force on the claim's date (`RateTable.floored`).
Null (shown as n/a) when no rate applies. | | Rate in force | `RateTable.on(grade, date)`. It uses the person's grade on the claim's date (`Person.gradeOn`) and the rate with the latest from-date on or before that date. It is null if that rate's to-date has passed. If the sheet has no rate, it falls back to the parent sheet's rates, up to 3 levels (`ParentRates`, `ANCESTOR_LEVELS`). | | Rounding | `RateTable.rounding(roundsBy)`: **HALF_UP before the policy date, HALF_EVEN on or after it**. With no policy date set, the sheet's today is used. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`correctsDate`). Displayed money is always `setScale(2, HALF_UP)`. | | **late charge** | `RateTable.lateCharge`. For each full 30 days (`LATE_PERIOD_DAYS`) past `graceBy`, it adds the `latePct` in force on that boundary date, applied to figure + earlier charges (so it **compounds**). Each step is rounded by `roundsBy`, and a 0% boundary adds nothing. | | **due-by** (`claim-due-by`) | Fixed when the claim is added: `HolidayService.businessDaysAfter(date, terms)`, skipping weekends and holidays. `terms` comes from `DatedSettings.termsFor`: the person's own terms, else the grade's terms on that date, else the sheet's (default 14). The claim keeps its `terms`. Adding a holiday later re-fixes due-by for every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday. Re-dating, editing or a later change of terms leaves it alone. | | **overdue** (`claim-overdue`) | `Dues.overdue`: the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `graceBy` (due-by + the grade's `grace` days on the claim's date) is before today. This per-claim flag does **not** check whether the claim counts, so a held claim can still show "yes". | | **deferred** (`claim-deferred`) | The view checks `deferredUntil > today` whatever the status. The counting rule `Dues.deferred` also requires OPEN, so the two do not quite agree. | | **stated** (`claim-stated`) | The last statement bound this claim. | | **counts** | `Dues.counts`: status is OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED (`ClaimStatus.counts`), the claim is not deferred, and it is not `leftOut`. `leftOut` applies to unbound claims only: an OPEN claim dated inside a hold, or an OPEN or PENDING claim once today ≥ the person's retirement date. | | **number** (`claim-number`) | Given when the claim is opened (`giveNumber`). Normally it is `FY-n`, by the fiscal year of the **due-by**, in one sequence shared by the whole sheet tree. While `periodNumberingFrom` ≤ today it is `-n` or `X-n` instead. Numbers are never reused, and a reassigned claim is renumbered. | | **period** (`claim-period`) | The period that contains the claim's **due-by**, not its date. | | Other flags | `lateEntry`: the claim was added while a soft-closed period contained its due-by. `proofs`, `remindedOn` (at most once per today), `splitFrom`, `settleBatch`, `voidReason`, `lockedBy`. | ### Per person (`PersonView`, `person-*` testids) - **grade**: `gradeOn(today)`. - **claimed**: `Dues.claimed`, the sum of amounts of claims that count, leaving out corrections. - **due-total**: `Dues.total`, which is `uncapped` held to the **cap** in force on today (`RateTable.capped`). - `uncapped` is the sum of the due figures of claims that count. - It is **n/a** when today's grade has no rate, unless some counting claim has a "kept" figure or one made at another grade's rate. (`uncapped` has extra wording for the case where the rate has merely ended.) - **excess**: uncapped − cap. - **settledTotal / openTotal**: `Dues.part`, the SETTLED part versus the OPEN+PENDING part. These are never n/a. - **overdueCount / overdueTotal**: `Dues.overdue(list)`, which keeps only claims that count *and* are overdue. - **active**: an OPEN or PENDING claim that counts and is dated in the 30 days up to and including today. - **recentSettled**: frozen figures of SETTLED claims **dated** in the last 90 days (it goes by claim date, not settle date). - **aged 0–30 / 31–60 / 61+**: OPEN and PENDING claims that count, bucketed by days since the claim's date (a claim dated after today counts as age 0). - **statements**: count, last due-total and last date (`Statements`). - **held**: true if the person has any hold, whatever its dates. - **retired** / **retiredNow**: whether a retirement date is set (`isRetired`) / whether today ≥ that date (`retiredOn`). - Also shown: clashing, origin, retirements and snapshot lines (due-total on each day left behind). - **backing**: worked out **only in the front end** (frontend: `features/people/people.ts` `patronage`). It is patrons' `recentSettled` × equal shares, with the shares rounded half-even and the remainder going to the first-named patron. - **cut-total**: also front-end only; it adds up the person's pool cuts (see Pools below). ### Sheet totals - `Rollup.figures`: claimed-total is a plain sum. - Due-total and overdue-total use `trimmedSum`. With 3 or more people, the single highest and single lowest are dropped, and n/a people are skipped. - The front end recomputes the same trimming (`dueTotalOf`, `overdueTotalOf`). - **consolidated** adds these over the sheet's descendant sheets. - Rollup also writes an alert when a person's due-total crosses above `alertThreshold`. - Summary (frontend: `features/summary/summary.ts`), all computed in the browser: - **by grade**: leaves out retired people, using `retired`, which is true whenever a date is set. - **by period**: each period's total and its change from the period before. - **by month**: the dues of claims that count, grouped by the claim's date. - **by status** and **by void reason**: counts. ### What freezes, and when - **Settle or approve** fixes `settledDue` = `Dues.figure` at that moment, with the late charge frozen in. - **Re-settle** (steward only) re-fixes it with `Dues.asOpen`: today's rate, floor and late charge, ignoring any statement. - **Statement** (`StatementService.take`): - Binds every counting claim to its **base** only. The late charge and floor stay live. - Releases every other claim. PENDING claims are never bound. - Can be taken as of a past date, using `DayEnds` to rebuild the sheet as it was. - Cancelling (steward only) unbinds every claim; earlier statements are not restored. - Splitting or reassigning a claim also unbinds it. - **Period close** (`PeriodService.fix`): - For each person, adds up the figures of claims whose **due-by** is in the period and whose status at the end of the period's last day counted (`Dues.countsAsOf`). - The figures are *today's* figures, and deferral and hold/retirement exclusions are judged on *today*. - The total is stored in `personTotals` and `closedTotal`. - **Soft-close** fixes the totals the same way but still allows changes. - **Reopen** makes the totals live again. - When today moves and `graceDays` is set, open periods with to + grace < today are closed automatically. - **Closed (hard) period**: `requireOpen(dueBy)` refuses add, edit, lock, move, delete, restore, defer, redate, split, addLine, addProof, approve, reject, resettle and reassign. Comment and remind are still allowed. - **Period cap**: an OPEN claim cannot be opened if the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims due in the period. ### Who may do what - **Roles** (`Role`): clerk by default; steward; viewer. - A user acts as steward while today falls inside a delegation to them. Only a steward by role (not by delegation) can delegate. - **Viewer**: every change is refused, and so is every change on an **archived** sheet (`ViewerGuard`, which works by URL pattern; bulk actions pass through and report every item as refused). - **Permission matrix** (`Permission`, setting `perm-`, blank means the standing rule): - open, settle, void and close: clerk and steward; - reassign and reopen: steward. - **Steward only, hard-coded**: - approve and reject PENDING claims; - re-settle; re-date; - void a SETTLED claim, within 7 days of its last SETTLED log date; - cancel a statement; - merge, transfer, clone and archive. - **Clerk limit**: a clerk settling a claim whose due is above the `clerkLimit` in force on **today** leaves it **PENDING** (`AccessService.canSettle`). An n/a due is always within the limit. - The person who **opened** or **last edited** a claim cannot settle or approve it. - **Proof threshold**, judged on the **claim date**: the grade's threshold, else the sheet's. A claim above it with 0 proofs cannot be settled or approved. - **Note threshold**: a claim above it with an empty note cannot be opened. - **Status moves** (`ClaimStatus.canBecome`): - DRAFT → OPEN; OPEN → SETTLED or PENDING; anything except DELETED → VOID. - Only a DRAFT can be edited or deleted. A DELETED claim can be restored only on the same today it was deleted. - Only an OPEN claim can be deferred (to a date after today) or split. - A deferred claim cannot be settled or split. - **Void reasons**: while the sheet's list is non-empty, a void needs a reason from it. - **References**: unique on the sheet, ignoring case. ### What a date decides - **Sheet `today`** decides: - overdue and late charge, cap, clerk limit; - the grade shown, active, aged, recentSettled; - deferral, retiredNow; - pool membership dates and holds for cuts; - delegation and the permission setting. - **Claim date** decides: - rate, grade, floor, grace, terms; - proof and note thresholds; - holds; - the rounding mode (via the policy date). - **Due-by** decides the period, closed-period refusals, the fiscal-year number and the period cap. - **Entry date**, when set, replaces today as the default claim date (`SheetService.claimDate`). - **Changing today**: - releases every editor lock; - snapshots the day being left (`DayEnds`, `SheetPasts`, `PersonSnapshots`); - auto-closes periods that are past their grace days. - **As-of view** (`AsOfFilter`): the sheet is read as it stood at the end of that date, and every change is refused. ### Holds, retirement, imports, pools - **Hold** (`HoldSpan.covers`, both ends included): - only *unbound OPEN* claims **dated** inside the hold drop out of the totals; - PENDING and SETTLED claims are unaffected; - a hold covering today gives a 0.00 pool cut. - **Retirement**: - once today ≥ `retiredFrom`, unbound OPEN and PENDING claims drop out; - a claim dated **after** `retiredFrom` is refused, as is one strictly inside a past retirement (`RetirementSpan.bars`); - a retired person cannot be merged or transferred. - **Imports** are all-or-nothing and return a count: - `PersonImportService`: a matching name or alias updates that person, with the grade recorded from today; anything else adds a person. - `PasteClaimsService`: makes DRAFTs; a ` #ref` at the end of the note becomes the reference. - `RateImportService`. - **Bulk actions**: - bulk settle is all-or-nothing and gets the next batch number; a claim left PENDING still counts as settled; - open, redate, reassign, grade and retire go one item at a time, so a refused item does not stop the rest. - **Plans** generate DRAFTs up to today and skip dates the claim form refuses. **Quick-add** creates the person, with grade A, if the name is new. - **Pools** (`Pools`): - a pool is balanced when its shares total exactly 100.00; - cut = pot × share ÷ the shares of members who get a cut, rounded half-even; - the remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut, the latest-added on a tie; - retired members and members on hold today get 0.00; - members whose dates don't include today are left out entirely; - nested pools go at most 3 deep. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It was mixed, leaning tangled: - **The figure maths is in one good place.** `Dues` + `RateTable` + `DatedSettings`, with honest Javadoc, is something a newcomer could pick up. - **Everything around it is scattered.** "Who may do what" and "what's refused" are inline checks spread through the ~1000-line `ClaimService`, plus `AccessService`, a URL-pattern `ViewerGuard`, `PeriodService` and `Person`. - **The front end re-implements server rules:** period totals, hold and retirement exclusion, trimmed sums. Some figures (backing, cut-total, the summary tables) exist only in the browser. - **The comments have drifted from the code.** For example: - the `ClaimView` doc describes due-by as "date plus terms", but it is business days; - the periods component says "date falls in it" while the code uses due-by; - `addProof` says "dated inside" a closed period but checks due-by; - the two "deferred" checks disagree on status. So you can't trust the docs without reading the code.
